message.reasoning:
I'm planning a thorough JUnit 4 test suite for the CharacterReader class, covering constructors, position tracking, consumption methods, marking/rewinding, and the various nextIndexOf/consumeTo overloads.

I also want tests for the matching helpers (matches, matchesAny, matchesLetter, matchesDigit, matchConsume) plus the rangeEquals test helper, keeping everything in the org.jsoup.parser package since many members are package-private. I'll include large-input tests to exercise the internal buffering logic, since the buffer size caps at 32768 characters with a 24576 read-ahead limit, making sure consumption past the buffer split point triggers correct refills.

I'm also planning a constructor test using a custom Reader that overrides markSupported to return false, expecting an IllegalArgumentException, plus a null-input test assuming Validate.notNull throws similarly. From there I'm sketching out a full list of individual test methods covering construction, emptiness checks, current/consume behavior at boundaries, and basic advance/unconsume operations.

Beyond those, I'm outlining tests for marking and rewinding, index-of searches for both single characters and sequences (including a case where the loop must iterate past a partial match), and consumption methods that stop at specific characters, strings, or sets of delimiters—covering both found and not-found branches, including sorted character sets. I'm also listing tests for consumeData's stop conditions, tag name parsing, consuming to end, letter sequences, letter-then-digit sequences, and hex sequences.

Continuing on, I'm covering matching methods for single characters, strings (including too-long cases), case-insensitive matching, character sets, sorted sets, letters, digits, and the consume-and-match variants, plus containsIgnoreCase and toString and rangeEquals edge cases. I'm also planning a test for string caching behavior when strings exceed the max cache length, and a test that forces the buffer to reload multiple times with a very large input to verify position tracking stays correct.

I'm also noting an edge case: calling consumeToAny with no characters at all means the inner loop never triggers a break, so it should consume the entire remaining buffer—worth testing explicitly. Similarly, consumeToAnySorted with an empty array would always return a negative binary search result, so it should behave the same way and consume to the end.

Beyond that, I want to cover nextIndexOf when the sequence is just one character matching right at the start, consumeTo returning an empty string when the match is at offset zero, matches() failing when the scan length exceeds the remaining buffer near the end of input, and matchConsume falling through to false when a partial match at the end isn't long enough. I should also check Character.isLetter() behavior for unicode letters.

I'm now thinking through how consumeLetterThenDigitSequence behaves when letters run all the way to the end of the buffer with no digits, triggering the isEmptyNoBufferUp() check in the digit loop, plus a separate case where digits actually follow. Then I'll start writing the actual JUnit4 test code.

Writing constructor exception tests...

I should test letter determination with a non-ASCII letter like 'é' to confirm Java's Character.isLetter treats it correctly, plus check hex sequences with trailing non-hex characters and simple digit sequences. For a mixed case like "abc123xyz", the method should return the concatenated letters-then-digits "abc123" before stopping at the non-digit 'x'.

For a pure-letter input like "abc" with no trailing digits, the digit loop should break immediately since bufPos equals bufLength. I also want to verify consumeData halts properly at '&', '<', and the null character, that consumeTagName stops at whitespace, '/', '>', '<', and null, and that nextIndexOf correctly scans forward through a buffer to locate a matching subsequence.

That confirms the boundary branch returns -1 correctly when offset reaches bufLength. Next I want to check that consumeTo(String) falls through to consumeToEnd() when the target isn't found, and verify cacheString bypasses its cache for strings longer than 12 characters by testing a 20-character token with consumeToAny and no delimiters present. Testing actual hash collisions in cacheString isn't feasible without internal access, so I'll just note that as a black-box limitation.

I realize rangeEquals is package-private, so I can call it directly from the same-package test class to hit its length-mismatch, content-mismatch, and match branches explicitly. I also want to exercise bufferUp's refill logic by feeding a 40000-character string through a CharacterReader backed by a StringReader, forcing multiple internal buffer loads as I consume the content in a loop.

I should verify pos() tracking stays correct throughout, and that isEmpty() and pos()==length hold once fully consumed. I also want to test constructing CharacterReader with an oversized buffer size to confirm the internal cap to maxBufferLen doesn't break functional behavior, plus edge cases like an empty string input and a Reader that always returns EOF to check markSupported-false handling.

I'll also cover boundary cases for matches and matchesIgnoreCase where the scan length exceeds remaining buffer content (expecting false), and test matchConsumeIgnoreCase for both matching and non-matching branches, plus containsIgnoreCase for both found and not-found scenarios.

I also want to cover edge cases where consumption methods hit a delimiter immediately and return empty strings - consumeToAny, consumeToAnySorted, consumeData, consumeTagName, letter sequences, and hex/digit sequences all need tests for the start==bufPos branch. This feels comprehensive enough now, so I'll finalize the test code, making sure it compiles correctly against jsoup's actual internal API since this class lives within the jsoup source tree itself.

Writing JUnit test methods...

Now I need to verify the remaining method signatures carefully - matches, matchesIgnoreCase, matchesAny, matchesAnySorted (takes char[] not varargs), matchConsume variants, and consumeToAny/consumeToAnySorted, noting the sorted-array variant relies on binarySearch so I need to pass properly sorted arrays in my test calls.

I'm aiming for around 45 test methods to achieve thorough branch coverage, with comments in Thai, before writing out the final complete answer.
